newsitem.title: UK: INSTANT VIEW - UK PRODUCER PRICES.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - UK PRODUCER PRICES.

text.p: Following is a selection of analysts' comments about British producer prices. Input prices fell a seasonally adjusted 0.4 percent in July and an unadjusted 9.0 percent year-on-year. Output prices edged up 0.2 percent and were 1.4 percent higher than a year earlier.

"The picture is confirmed that the strength of sterling is killing input prices at the moment while the strength of domestic demand is allowing output prices to creep up. At the moment, the strength of sterling is winning out overall."

"What's interesting is the difference between the core rate of output prices and the headline rate. That suggests some of the budget effects have been passed through. That may be modestly bullish for prices in the medium term. The core index is key and has come in flat yet again. That very much suggests manufacturing selling prices will remain very soft for some time to come. But the real risk is that the service sector deteriorates. Even if manufacturing does not generate any significant inflationary pressures there is still very much a risk from the palpably more important services side."

"It's pretty much as expected although input prices could have fallen further with the four percent rise in the currency in July. Even so, it's nine percent down on a year ago, very subdued. Core output prices are flat. We're probably close to the trough in producer price inflation. But at such a low level, it's not a cause for concern. It's not that that is worrying the Bank of England, it's the pace of consumer demand.
NEIL PARKER, ROYAL BANK OF SCOTLAND

"July PPI data were in line with market forecasts. This shouldn't concern gilts or short sterling, and the upward pressure on headline output prices was due to the budget rises in petrol duties. RPI on Tuesday will show a tick up on the headline rate due to rises in mortgage rates. But we forecast RPIX at 2.7 percent, below the market consensus."
